Ape-like human ancestors underwent several modifications during the course of evolution to develop into present day humans which are summarized below. i. Walking on two legs (bipedal locomotion) and not using the forelimbs for walking on the ground. ii. Losing the ability to opposably use the big toes. iii. Adopting an upright posture by developing the lower back curve. iv. Growing a larger and more complex brain. v. Decreasing the size of eyebrow ridges, canine teeth, and incisor teeth. vi. Developing a distinct chin.

7.4.5 EVOLUTION OF MODERN MAN

The palentological evidence suggests that man originated in Central Asia, China, Java and India (Shivalik Hills). An established theory suggests Dryopithecus to be one of the oldest fossils that later evolved into apes and man. The origin and evolution of man can be understood in the following major headings:

Figure: 7.4.4 Timeline of evolution of man (with cranial capacity) 1. Dryopithecus or Proconsul The fossil of Dryopithecus africanus, that lived 15 million years ago, was discovered from Miocene rocks of Lake of Victoria, Africa and Europe by Leakey. It is regarded as a common ancestor of man and apes. Its characteristic features are listed below: i. They were hairy and looked more like an ape but walked like a gorilla and chimpanzee. ii. They were arboreal that fed on leaves and soft fruits. iii. They had round forehead like modern man but canine teeth were like apes. iv. They had forelimbs that were weaker and shorter than hind limbs. v. The characteristics shown by the fossils indicates that they are not the direct ancestor of humans.
Figure: 7.4.5 Figure Proconsul Biology, Grade 11 | 277

2. Ramapithecus It is believed that in the late Miocene epoch, Dryopithecus gave rise to Ramapithecus which was on the direct line of human evolution. Thus, it appeared about 14 - 15 million years ago. Its fossil was discovered from Pliocene rocks of Shivalik Hills (India) by Edward Lewis and from Africa by Leaky. Its teeth were found in Dang valley, now preserved in the Natural History Museum, Kathmandu. Ramapithecus is assumed to be in the direct line of human evolution according to fossil records.

Some of its characteristic features are listed below: i. They were hairy and looked more like a man but walked like gorillas and chimpanzees. ii. They had small canine teeth but large molar teeth. It suggests, like modern man, Ramapithecus ate hard nuts and seeds.

(There is a GAP between Ramapithecus and Australopithecus which is not described, yet). 3. Australopithecus (First ape man). Australopithecus evolved as the first human-like form that existed around 2 million years ago. The fossil of Australopithecus (African Ape man) was discovered by Raymond Dart in South Africa from the Pleistocene rock. Australopithecus was of two species: A. africanus and A. robustus.

Some of the characteristic A. africanus are listed below: i. They had erect posture more like a man and walked upright without chin ii. They had an ape-like brain (500 cc) and man-like teeth with brow ridges projected over the eyes. iii. Evidence suggests them to have hunting life and used stones, sticks, bones as hunting weapons. iv. Their canine teeth were smaller than that of apes v. They were omnivorous but mainly fed on fruits.

It is believed that Australopithecus africanus later gave rise to Homo habilis. Do You Know? Donald Johanson discovered a 3.2 million years old skeleton of a female human ancestor of Australopithecus - Lucy (A. afarensis).
